title: Multiplying by Z to the alpha preserves back-and-forth relations with a doubled shift
author: David Gonzalez; Dino Rossegger
work: Scott sentence complexities of linear orderings
difficulty_reason: Counted unit is the author labelled lemma at source0.tex lines 1275-1278: for any two countable linear orders, a rank beta comparison between them yields a comparison of rank twice alpha plus beta between their products with Z^alpha. The statement is a rank arithmetic assertion with no witness, and the proof (source lines 1280-1301) has to run an induction on beta in which the successor step is the real work: the product is rewritten as an ordering of pairs, the opponent plays a tuple of pairs, the answer is produced coordinatewise by the winning strategy of the original comparison, and the interval that remains to be compared is identified with a concatenation of two zeta blocks around the product of the corresponding interval, after which the induction hypothesis applies. Neither the coordinatewise strategy nor the interval computation is visible in the statement, and the doubled shift in the rank comes out of the second factor.
